dedupe_keys.name: american red cross west africa project community survey and mapping along the guinea liberia and sierra leone borders 2016

description: From February to October 2016 the American Red Cross and the Red Cross societies of Guinea, Liberia and Sierra Leone mapped the area within 15 kilometres of the three countries' shared borders, to give decision makers and responders an open dataset of communities and of water, sanitation, health and other community resources before the next crisis. Working from a mapping centre in Guéckédou, Guinea, more than 100 volunteers visited over 7,000 communities by motorbike to complete a vulnerability survey with each village leader, and then mapped every water point, health facility and other community resource in more than 100 selected communities. Access: the rapid assessment survey as CSV and Stata files with a data dictionary, final and methodology reports, and the project area as GeoJSON and Shapefile on HDX. Licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0, except the OpenStreetMap extracts; free. Caveats: personally identifiable information was removed, some community locations are wrong although their survey answers are correct, and files should be opened as UTF-8. Simulation uses are community-level locations of health facilities and water points in a rural border region for emergency response, access and service coverage modelling. Related records: HOT OpenStreetMap exports and Healthsites.io.
